long_biography.plain_text:
At Agria Group Holding, Emil Raykov built a vertically integrated position in Bulgarian agriculture. From farms in the north-east, the group expanded by acquiring smaller producers, adding grain stores and processing assets, and building trading and export capacity around Black Sea ports.

Raykov has led Agria as chairman and chief executive since its formation as a public-company platform. Its operating chain links cultivation and leased land to storage, oilseed processing, logistics and international grain sales. In 2025, the group established a Swiss commodities subsidiary to extend cereal and oilseed trading across the Black Sea and Danube region, reinforcing trade as the centre of Raykov's business.

Search results for an Emil Raykov born in 1958 refer to a Bulgarian opera singer, while other LinkedIn results lack Agria's full identity markers; none of their facts were transferred.

The original exchange prospectus contains an official personal identifier, but the dossier does not reproduce it or infer a birth date from it. A hostile anonymous blog supplies a date and place of birth without independent reliable corroboration, so the blank birth day, month, year and place remain unproposed.

Primary company material directly documents Raykov's creation of a consultancy, subsequent fuel-trading company and role in building the present group, supporting broad Self-made. It does not establish his family finances, networks or source of initial capital, so neither the independent-start nor advantaged-start subtype is selected.

Raykov's companies and shareholdings helped create the platform that became Agria, but other shareholders and managers also participated in the predecessor businesses. Operator is therefore used as the current primary relationship because his sustained executive control is explicit, without overstating sole founder status.

The exact percentage held through Emra has changed over time and is intentionally omitted from the biographies. First-party and brokerage disclosures consistently establish Emra as a leading or majority shareholder at the relevant dates and identify it as wholly owned by Raykov, which is sufficient for the durable major-shareholder description.

The existing LinkedIn URL is verified by the official Agria management page and is not proposed again. Focused searches found no personal Instagram, Facebook, X, YouTube, TikTok or personal website that met the identity threshold; search results included unrelated same-name people.
No dedicated Forbes profile or credible exact-person Forbes result was found in the required exact-profile-first and follow-up Agria searches.

Agricultural production is central to Raykov's profile, but the active catalogue has no approved literal whose contract captures general crop-farming ownership more cleanly. Commodity trading is assigned because grain and oilseed trade is a long-running, material and current operating specialism; food manufacturing and renewable energy are omitted as secondary or overlapping exposures.
